> **What this case shows** — a heartbeat can be sensed two utterly different ways:
> **optically**, as the pulse of blood volume in the finger (the photoplethysmogram,
> **PPG**), and **electrically**, as the heart's depolarization (the **ECG**). If both
> measure the same heart, they should share a rhythm — and **magnitude-squared
> coherence** proves it, quantifying the frequency-resolved linear coupling between two
> signals in [0, 1]. On a real simultaneous recording the PPG–ECG coherence peaks at
> **0.898 at 1.465 Hz** — exactly **88 beats per minute**, the subject's heart rate —
> far above the 95% significance limit (0.026). The ecosystem's `coherence` reproduces
> the canonical **`scipy.signal.coherence`** to **machine precision** (max |diff| =
> 2.9×10⁻¹⁴ over the full spectrum, with the Welch settings matched exactly).

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for two signals: `coherence(x, y, sr, nperseg, noverlap)` → read the
**coherence spectrum** and its **95% confidence limit** → find the peak in the band of
interest.
**Way of thinking** — coherence is the *linear frequency-domain* coupling: a peak at a
frequency means the two signals share a rhythm there. Always read it against the
confidence limit (coherence is biased upward with few segments), and mind the
pre-processing — without detrending, a DC/baseline component dominates, so read the
finding in a physiological band.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioCrossModal::coherence()` (magnitude / imaginary / lagged),
`multitaperCoherence()`, `waveletCoherence()`, `wPLI()` for the rest of the connectivity
toolkit.
:::

## Proposition

On a real simultaneous PPG + ECG recording (BIDMC subject 01), the magnitude-squared
coherence peaks at 0.898 at 1.465 Hz (88 bpm — the heart rate), and `coherence`
reproduces `scipy.signal.coherence` to machine precision (max |diff| = 2.9×10⁻¹⁴).

## Question & goal

**The question is whether two different cardiac sensors share a rhythm, and whether the
ecosystem measures coherence exactly.** Coherence is a Welch-based computation with
several conventions (window, overlap, detrend), so a "correct" implementation must be
pinned to a reference. The goal is a head-to-head against `scipy.signal.coherence` and a
clear physiological read: do PPG and ECG cohere at the heart rate?

## Challenge & approach

Coherence via Welch depends on the window and detrending. We match those exactly and
compare the whole spectrum to scipy; then we read the peak in the cardiac band, where
the PPG and ECG — both driven by the heartbeat — should lock together.

```
PPG ┐
    ├─ coherence (Welch, sym-Hann, no detrend) → spectrum  (== scipy.signal.coherence)
ECG ┘        peak in the cardiac band (0.5–5 Hz) → heart rate
```

## Data

**BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset (PhysioNet)**: subject bidmc01, the simultaneous
**PLETH (PPG)** and **lead-II (ECG)** at 125 Hz, first 4 min. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the PPG–ECG coherence spectrum (0–10 Hz); it peaks sharply at 1.465 Hz (88 bpm, red dot) — the heart rate — with harmonics above; the dotted line is the 95% confidence limit. Right: the ecosystem's coherence against scipy.signal.coherence, frequency by frequency, on the identity line (max |diff| = 2.9×10⁻¹⁴).](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* a coherence peak at a frequency means the two signals share a rhythm
there. The sharp peak at the heart rate says the optical and electrical views of the
heart are locked to the same beat; the right panel shows the two tools are numerically
identical.

| Quantity | This reproduction | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| max \|diff\| vs scipy (full spectrum) | **2.9×10⁻¹⁴** | 0 (identical) |
| Cardiac-band peak coherence | **0.898** | — |
| Peak frequency | **1.465 Hz (88 bpm)** | — |
| Band-mean coherence (0.5–5 Hz) | **0.439** | — |

The op reproduces scipy exactly, and the PPG and ECG cohere strongly at the heart rate.
Values trace to
[`artifacts/coherence_summary.csv`](artifacts/coherence_summary.csv) and the spectrum in
[`artifacts/coherence_spectrum.csv`](artifacts/coherence_spectrum.csv).

## Conclusion

The optical and electrical views of the heart are locked to the same beat, and the
ecosystem's coherence measures that coupling exactly as scipy does. The transferable
takeaway: **coherence is the linear frequency-domain coupling — read it against the
confidence limit and in a physiological band (detrending matters), and validate it
against the canonical tool by matching the Welch settings, or the numbers will differ.**

## Open questions

- Coherence at the heart rate confirms a shared cardiac rhythm; the **respiratory band**
  (RESP is also recorded) would map **cardiorespiratory coupling**, and the
  **imaginary/lagged coherence** (also implemented) would separate genuine coupling from
  zero-lag/volume-conduction artefacts. Extending to **corticomuscular / intermuscular**
  coherence, or to a per-segment-detrended spectrum for the low-frequency couplings,
  would turn the validated coherence op into a connectivity study. *Documented, not
  escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| magnitude-squared coherence | `coherence()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| multitaper coherence | `multitaperCoherence()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| wavelet (time-frequency) coherence | `waveletCoherence()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| phase-lag connectivity (volume-conduction robust) | `wPLI()` | PhysioCrossModal |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **nperseg / noverlap** — longer segments give finer frequency resolution but fewer
  segments (noisier coherence); 50% overlap is standard. Here 512 (4 s) resolves the
  heart rate.
- **confidence_limit** — always compare the coherence to the returned 95% limit; with
  few segments coherence is biased upward.
- **detrend / band** — the op does not detrend, so a DC/baseline component appears; read
  the coherence in a physiological band, or pre-detrend the signals.
- **type** — use `"imaginary"` or `"lagged"` coherence when zero-lag/volume-conduction
  coupling must be excluded (e.g. EEG connectivity).

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioCrossModal)

# x, y = two aligned numeric signals, sr in Hz
co <- coherence(x, y, sr = 125, nperseg = 512, noverlap = 256)
band <- co$frequencies >= 0.5 & co$frequencies <= 5      # cardiac band
pk <- which(band)[which.max(co$coherence[band])]
co$coherence[pk]          # 0.898  -- peak coherence
co$frequencies[pk] * 60   # 88 bpm -- the shared heart rate

# exact by construction: matches scipy.signal.coherence with matched Welch settings
# (symmetric-Hann window, detrend = FALSE).
```
